_note: System data format v1.0 — Terra (Solo/0827) as the worked example. Every field is present; null means the data exists but is unknown or not yet supplied. dataSource tracks the origin of each value: 'derived' (calculated from world UWP/PBG/stellar), 'rolled' (generated by Traveller system generation rules), 'canonical' (real-world or published Traveller data). A canonical override replaces any derived or rolled value for the same field.
name: Terra
_note_stars: One entry per stellar entry in world.stellar[]. The primary star is always index 0. Companion stars also appear in the orbits array so their orbital position can be recorded.

stars._note_stellarClass: Derived from luminosity class (V = main-sequence, IV = subgiant, III = giant, II = bright-giant, Ia/Ib = supergiant, D = white-dwarf)
stars._note_color: Derived from spectral class letter (O=blue, B=blue-white, A=white, F=yellow-white, G=yellow, K=orange, M=red)
stars._note_radiusScale: Relative to Sol = 1.0. Derived from spectral class + luminosity class. Unknown until lookup table is built.
stars._note_habitableZone: Derived from STAR_HZ table in orbitData.ts. inner/outer are AU bounds. G2 V hz ≈ 3 (orbit id 3 = 1.0 AU)
stars._note_orbitId_companion: null for the primary. Companion stars reference their orbital slot in the orbits array.

_note_orbits: Bodies with a known orbital position. orbitId maps to orbits.json (index 0–20). zone is derived from comparison of orbitId to the star's habitableZone.orbitId. Bodies we know exist but cannot place are in unplaced[].

orbits._note: Main world — orbit derived from star HZ lookup. Terra sits at orbitId 3 = 1.0 AU, matching G2 V habitable zone.

body.name: Terra
body._note_atmosphereType: Derived from uwp.atmosphere code. Vocabulary: none | trace | very-thin | thin | standard | dense | exotic | corrosive | insidious
body._note_surfaceType: Derived from uwp.hydrographics + trade codes. Vocabulary: barren | desert | arid | terran | ocean | ice | exotic | hellworld
body._note_tradeCodes: From world.remarks. Used to refine surface rendering (Ga=garden, De=desert, Wa=water world, Ic=ice, Va=vacuum, Fl=fluid oceans, He=hellworld, Fr=frozen)
body._note_axialTilt: Not derivable from world data. Required for visual orientation of poles and rings.
body._note_rotationPeriodH: Not derivable from world data. Required for day/night animation speed.
body._note_canonicalTexture: Path to a pre-generated texture overriding procedural generation. Set for known worlds like Terra.
body._note_moons: Not derivable from world data. Count, size, and position of natural satellites are all unknown.
body._note_hasRings: Not derivable. Null = unknown, false = confirmed none, true = confirmed rings present.

_note_belt_main_world: When uwp.size = 0 the main world is an asteroid belt. The belt occupies the HZ orbit slot directly in orbits[] with isMainWorld: true. No parent body is needed. Belt entries that are the main world carry name, tradeCodes, and isMainWorld just like a world body. Example: { kind: 'belt', isMainWorld: true, name: 'Examplename', tradeCodes: ['As'], orbitId: 3, au: 1.0, zone: 'habitable' }
_note_satellite_pattern: The main world always orbits the primary — either directly, or via a parent body that itself orbits the primary. Maximum one level of nesting. If the main world is a satellite, its parent body occupies the HZ orbit slot in orbits[] and the main world appears in that parent's moons[] with isMainWorld: true. _note_unplaced: Bodies we know exist from PBG/worldsInSystem but whose orbital position is unknown. The renderer places these procedurally until canonical or rolled data fills in orbitId. Count: gasGiants from pbg.gasGiants, belts from pbg.belts, otherWorlds = worldsInSystem - 1 (main world) - gasGiants - belts.

unplaced._note_gasGiantType: Determined by rolling on gg.json table. SGG (rolls 1-4), LGG (rolls 5-12+). Every 2nd SGG in sequence is converted to IG. Drives which p2 column is used for orbit placement.
unplaced._note_sizeCode: Letter code L-Y from gg.json roll. Determines diameter and gravity.

_note_counts: Summary derived from world data. Used to validate that orbits + unplaced add up correctly.
_note_infrastructure: Derived from world.bases. Implies orbital installations the renderer may eventually show.
